walkthroughs.body_html:
The Early Stuarts & the Origins of the Civil War 1603-1660 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Early Stuarts & the Origins of the Civil War 1603-1660 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Early Stuarts & the Origins of the Civil War 1603-1660.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What caused the English Civil War?
options: It was caused by Henry VIII's break with Rome.
It was caused by Charles I trying to arrest five MPs in 1642.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
Long-term tensions over royal absolutism, religion (Laudian reforms), and parliamentary rights, combined with Charles I's specific mismanagement and personal rigidity.
